ailment.batuk_debu.desc: A dry cough as if choked by dust; red eyes and a slow pulse.
ailment.batuk_debu.name: Dust Cough
ailment.demam_embun.desc: Shivering at dawn; a warm forehead and a quick pulse.
ailment.demam_embun.name: Dew Fever
ailment.kepala_kabut.desc: A foggy head with droopy eyes and a weak pulse.
ailment.kepala_kabut.name: Misty Head
ailment.kulit_getah.desc: An itchy rash as if touched by sap; yellow tongue, quick pulse.
ailment.kulit_getah.name: Sap Skin
ailment.kulit_lembap.desc: A damp rash and bloating; a sweaty forehead and a wavy pulse.

ailment.lambung_panas.desc: A tender, hot belly with a yellow tongue and a strong pulse.

ailment.mata_pasir.desc: Stinging eyes as if full of sand; red tongue, wavy pulse.
ailment.mata_pasir.name: Sandy Eyes
ailment.otot_tegang.desc: Tight, warm muscles with a red tongue and a strong pulse.
ailment.otot_tegang.name: Tense Muscles
ailment.perut_kabut.desc: A bloated, sluggish belly with a white tongue and a weak pulse.
ailment.perut_kabut.name: Misty Belly
ailment.sendi_karat.desc: Stiff joints as if rusted; a cool body and a slow pulse.
ailment.sendi_karat.name: Rusty Joints

dlg.chapter_later: Alright, another time when you're ready.
dlg.choice.chapter: I'd like to hear your story
dlg.choice.quest: Is there a task for me?
dlg.dewi.about: I love playing near the pond. The water is clear and cool.
dlg.dewi.about2: Mother says healers know all the medicinal leaves. Is that true?
dlg.dewi.ch1: I often slipped off to the river when my parents weren't looking. Once I saw a white heron there.
dlg.dewi.ch1_more: Since then I've wanted to know every faraway place around the village. But I'm scared to go alone.
dlg.dewi.ch2: I once got lost in the forest. Luckily I recognised a leaf from a book, so I could find my way home.
dlg.dewi.ch2_more: Since then I've learned to recognise plants as best I can. If you'd teach me, I'd be very happy.
dlg.dewi.t0: Healer! Have you been to the river? I'm so curious!
dlg.dewi.t1: Healer! Yesterday I saw a huge fish in the pond. Do you believe me?
dlg.dewi.t2: Healer, you're my best friend! I have a little secret, want to hear it?
dlg.joko.about: The pond in the north-east has plump fish. Mornings are best.
dlg.joko.about2: At noon I fetch water at the well, then go back to fishing.
dlg.joko.ch1: I've fished since I was small. My father said patience is half of the catch.
dlg.joko.ch1_more: This pond used to be a big river. Then its course changed, and I still haven't grown used to it.
dlg.joko.ch2: My wife was sick for a long time and no healer could help. Since then I've kept my distrust.
dlg.joko.ch2_more: Watching you work, I've begun to think things may be different now. But I'm not sure yet.
dlg.joko.greet: Shh, not so loud, you'll scare the fish.
dlg.joko.t1: Healer. The pond water is very calm today.
dlg.joko.t2: Healer, I rarely talk at length. But with you, I enjoy talking.
dlg.karto.about: I planted those leaves myself. The garden is open to you any time.
dlg.karto.about2: Morning is the best time to tend plants. At midday I rest in the square.
dlg.karto.ch1: Long ago I wandered far away. This garden is what brought me back to stay.
dlg.karto.ch1_more: My late wife planted the first cat's whiskers here. Since then I've tended them as her last wish.
dlg.karto.ch2: Behind the garden there's a wild patch I let grow. Rare plants once grew there.
dlg.karto.ch2_more: If you have time, try identifying what grows there. Maybe you can teach me something.
dlg.karto.greet: Welcome, Healer. The herb garden is thriving.
dlg.karto.t0: Good morning, Healer. My garden is still modest, but I water it every day.
dlg.karto.t1: Ah, Healer. Shall I show you the new leaves in my garden?
dlg.karto.t2: My favourite Healer! If you're not busy, sit under this tree first.
dlg.lastri.about: I go to the well early, then help out in the herb garden.
dlg.lastri.about2: The children play at the pond. I always worry when they lose track of time.
dlg.lastri.ch1: I have three children, and two of them love running into the forest. I'm always anxious.
dlg.lastri.ch1_more: I always make them bring water and food. That small habit has saved them more than once.
dlg.lastri.ch2: Once, when my youngest had a high fever, I came to the clinic in the middle of the night. You may not remember.
dlg.lastri.ch2_more: Since then I've wanted to repay you. If there's anything I can do for the village, just tell me.
dlg.lastri.greet: Welcome, Healer. Where have you been?
dlg.lastri.t0: Good afternoon, Healer. Don't forget to drink water.
dlg.lastri.t1: Healer, the children keep asking about you. They're in awe.
dlg.lastri.t2: Healer, if you need anything, just say so. We're all here for you.
dlg.no_request: Nothing for now. Thanks for asking, Healer.
dlg.patient.called: Called already? Alright, I'm heading to the exam room.
dlg.patient.coming: I'm on my way to the clinic. {complaint}
dlg.patient.leaving: Thank you, Healer. I'm going home now.
dlg.raka.about: I help Father in the garden and sometimes roam the village for news.
dlg.raka.about2: In the evening I like going to the pond. The view is lovely.
dlg.raka.ch1: I'm an orphan from across the river. I live here because Uncle Karto took me in.
dlg.raka.ch1_more: I want to be useful. That's why I help in the garden and go around the village.
dlg.raka.ch2: I once went to the mountains alone to prove myself. I nearly got hurt on a slippery slope.
dlg.raka.ch2_more: Since then I've learned patience. If you go out again, take me along. I promise I'll listen.
dlg.raka.greet: Oh, Healer! Need help carrying anything?
dlg.raka.t0: Healer! I just finished helping in the garden. Tiring, but fun!
dlg.raka.t1: Healer, I want to learn to recognise plants like you do. May I?
dlg.raka.t2: Healer, someday I want to be a healer too. Will you be my teacher?
dlg.ratih.about: Each morning I pick spices in the garden, then deliver them to the clinic before noon.
dlg.ratih.about2: The queue is usually busy in the afternoon. Be sure to open the clinic on time.
dlg.ratih.ch1: I used to be a nurse in the city. I moved here for a quieter place.
dlg.ratih.ch1_more: But in this village, people often delay seeing a healer until it's too late. That's what I fear most.
dlg.ratih.ch2: I once lost a patient because they were brought to a healer too late. Since then I've been strict about schedules.
dlg.ratih.ch2_more: Sorry if I'm harsh. I only want you not to repeat that mistake. You've shown that you care.
dlg.ratih.greet: Why, Healer. My spices are fresh today.
dlg.ratih.t0: Healer. Don't be late opening the clinic again.
dlg.ratih.t1: Healer, your work has been good lately. Keep it up.
dlg.ratih.t2: Healer, I rely on you. This village is lucky to have you, and I'm proud.
dlg.request_accepted: Thank you, Healer. I'll be waiting for your news.
dlg.request_claim: All done? Thank you so much, Healer!
dlg.request_declined: That's fine. Let me know if you find the time.
dlg.request_done: Thanks for helping, Healer. The village is lucky to have you.
dlg.request_pending: How about my request? Not done yet?
dlg.sari.about: I sell along the village road in the morning, then move to the square before noon.
dlg.sari.about2: Many villagers have started complaining of aches. Your clinic may get busy.
dlg.sari.ch1: I've traded since I was young. My mother was a travelling trader who went in and out of the forest for ingredients.
dlg.sari.ch1_more: From her I learned every herb's price, but never how to use them. That's why I respect you healers.
dlg.sari.ch2: Bad news often hits the market: prices rise, herbs run short. I'm afraid one day the village will run out of medicine.
dlg.sari.ch2_more: That's why I'm glad when you buy and store herbs wisely. It's worth more than you think.
dlg.sari.greet: Healer! What luck, do stop by.
dlg.sari.t0: Hello, Healer! Buying anything today? Or, um... just chatting first?
dlg.sari.t1: Healer! I just heard news from the market. Want to hear it?
dlg.sari.t2: Healer, you're like my own sibling. Come sit, I'll treat you to tea.
dlg.wiryo.about: This village was here long before I was born. That clinic used to be a small hut.
dlg.wiryo.about2: If you are unsure, ask the villagers how they are. Everyone has a story.
dlg.wiryo.ch1: I was a healer in this village once, before you learned to see leaves with your own eyes.
dlg.wiryo.ch1_more: Some plants heal when used correctly and harm when used carelessly. Remember that well.
dlg.wiryo.ch2: Long ago a woman healer wrote down every plant in a notebook. It was lost in the great flood.
dlg.wiryo.ch2_more: I still remember part of it. If you want, I'll help you recall what was lost.
dlg.wiryo.greet: Ah, young healer. Sit a while, child.
dlg.wiryo.t0: Oh, Healer. Sit a while, my legs can't stand for long anymore.
dlg.wiryo.t1: Healer, you're starting to understand how we live here, aren't you?
dlg.wiryo.t2: My child, I'm glad you came. There's something I've wanted to tell you for a long time.

sq.q_dewi_sungai.accepted: Yay! Don't forget, tell me the real story!
sq.q_dewi_sungai.done: Wow, how exciting! Thank you, Healer.
sq.q_dewi_sungai.offer: Go to the river and see for yourself. Then tell me about it!
sq.q_dewi_sungai.opt.apa_adanya: The river is calm, with driftwood along the banks and small flowers.
sq.q_dewi_sungai.opt.dilebihkan: The river is huge, and there's supposedly a giant crocodile! I nearly got hurt.
sq.q_dewi_sungai.title: A Story from the River
sq.q_dewi_sungai.turn: So, what's the river like? Tell me!
sq.q_dewi_sungai.wait: You haven't been to the river yet, have you? The path is east of the village.
sq.q_karto_kebun.done: Alright. I hope this garden becomes more useful for the village.
sq.q_karto_kebun.offer: Behind my garden there are plants I don't recognise. Could you identify two of them?
sq.q_karto_kebun.opt.ambil_pujian: I'm the one who identified them, so the credit is mine alone.
sq.q_karto_kebun.opt.bagi_jasa: Both of us, Uncle Karto. I identified them, you tended them.
sq.q_karto_kebun.title: Wild Plants in Karto's Garden
sq.q_karto_kebun.turn: You've identified the plants. Who should I credit for it?
sq.q_karto_kebun.wait: You haven't identified those two plants yet. I'm still waiting.
sq.q_ratih_pasien.accepted: Good. I'll wait for your report here.
sq.q_ratih_pasien.done: That's how a good healer does it. Keep it up.
sq.q_ratih_pasien.offer: Your work is getting neat. Treat three patients with good results, and the village benefits too.
sq.q_ratih_pasien.opt.bagi: Share it with the clinic helpers and teach them.
sq.q_ratih_pasien.opt.upah: I'll take my own pay. That's my right.
sq.q_ratih_pasien.title: Chosen Patients
sq.q_ratih_pasien.turn: You've treated patients well. How will the reward be shared?
sq.q_ratih_pasien.wait: Three patients with good results aren't done yet. Keep going.
sq.q_wiryo_ramuan.accepted: Thank you, Healer. Remember, only take what you truly recognise.
sq.q_wiryo_ramuan.done: Alright. The village will remember what you did.
sq.q_wiryo_ramuan.offer: Healer, please gather 3 herbs from the forest for me. I need them for tonight's remedy.
sq.q_wiryo_ramuan.opt.jujur: Record them exactly, some are already wilted.
sq.q_wiryo_ramuan.opt.untung: Sell them at market price. The customers won't know the difference.
sq.q_wiryo_ramuan.title: Herbs for Grandpa Wiryo
sq.q_wiryo_ramuan.turn: Got them? Let me see. How will you record these herbs?
sq.q_wiryo_ramuan.wait: The forest herbs aren't enough yet. Be patient.
